title: Follow-Up Visit Currency and Model Change Grants: Representative Training Notes, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
These training notes concern the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program and the effect of the customer's follow-up visit on the authorization grant Larkfield records for a new written order of the CGM supply allowance (A4239) that changes the CGM model under the payer authorization already in force.

**The rule.** The follow-up adjustment takes blocks off the grant by the follow-up visit, the most recent visit date on the program's medical records with purpose continued-need follow-up or initial qualification, a visit counting as current on a date when it is no more than the tier's follow-up visit interval in calendar months before that date, counted back with the same calendar day allowed (the last day of the month when that day does not exist), as the follow-up visit requirement for refills counts it:
- when the follow-up visit is current on the order date and is no longer current on the grant's valid-through date, it takes off one block for each whole calendar month from the follow-up visit date to the valid-through date beyond the interval;
- when the follow-up visit is no longer current on the order date, or no qualifying visit is on file at all, the grant carries no units until a new visit note is recorded (every block is taken off);
- otherwise, when the visit is current on both dates, it takes off no block.

**Q. Which visit is the follow-up visit?** The most recent visit date on the CGM program's medical records with purpose continued-need follow-up or initial qualification.

**Q. What is the interval on each tier?**

| Tier | Follow-up visit interval |
|---|---|
| CGM Self-Pay Program | 0 months |
| CGM Commercial HMO Program | 6 months |
| CGM Commercial PPO Program | 12 months |
| CGM Medicare Advantage Program | 6 months |
| CGM Original Medicare Program | 6 months |
| CGM Medicaid Program | 6 months |

**Q. How is "current on a date" counted?** Counting the interval back in calendar months from that date, with the same calendar day kept (or the last day of the month when that day does not exist), reaches a day; the visit is current on that date when its own date is on or after the day reached. With a 6-month interval, a visit on 10 January is current on 10 July and no longer current on 11 July. A visit on 28 February of a non-leap year is current on 31 August, because six months back from 31 August reaches 28 February.

**Q. What is a whole calendar month between two dates?** Whole calendar months from one date to a later date are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's calendar day is earlier than the earlier date's calendar day. From 10 January to 31 October is 9 whole months; from 10 January to 9 October is 8.

**Q. How many blocks does a lapse inside the grant take off?** The whole calendar months from the visit date to the grant's valid-through date, less the interval, one block for each. Hypothetical figures, with a 6-month interval, a visit on 10 January and an order dated 1 March (the visit is current on the order date):

| Grant valid through | Current on that date? | Whole months from the visit | Blocks taken off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 July | yes | 6 | none (still current) |
| 11 July | no | 6 | none (no whole month beyond 6) |
| 10 August | no | 7 | 1 |
| 31 October | no | 9 | 3 |

**Q. And when the visit is already out of date on the order date?** With the same 6-month interval, a visit on 10 January is no longer current on an order dated 11 July; the grant then carries no units until a new visit note is recorded.

**Q. And when the program has no qualifying visit at all?** When the CGM program's medical records carry no visit with purpose continued-need follow-up or initial qualification, the grant carries no units until a new visit note is recorded, exactly as when the visit is out of date on the order date.
